decisions.finding: First consonant initial Vav of וַיַּשְׁלִיכוּ sits at rows 1080..1151, cols 1500..1535 of extension-volumeA-591-zoom4-upper-right.png. Directly beneath the base of Vav at rows 1153..1165 sits a clear horizontal bar (width 25 px, height 14 px, dense ink pixels) forming an unmistakable Patah (ַ, U+05B7). Note is retired and Patah restored to Vav.

First consonant initial Vav of ויְהִי sits at rows 1079..1149, cols 780..815 of extension-volumeA-591-zoom4-upper-right.png. Offline inspection of the sublinear band across cols 780..815, rows 1150..1180 reveals zero ink pixels (100% pure white paper). Second consonant Yod bears a clear Sheva beneath it at rows 1150..1156. The initial Vav is an unpointed consonant (none) in the printed text, leaving ויְהִי correctly spelled with bare Vav. Note is retired as unpointed consonant.

Third consonant Yod of דָּנִיֵאל sits at cols 923..933, rows 1620..1642 of extension-volumeA-591-zoom4-upper-left.png on Line 11. Yod consists of a compact hook suspended from the roofline. Offline pixel inspection of the Yod body and surrounding cavity across cols 918..936, rows 1618..1650 reveals zero internal or crook ink; cols 919..926 are 100% unprinted white paper. Sublinear Tzere (ֵ) is stamped underneath at rows 1695..1706. No Dagesh dot is present in Yod in Kahana printed text. Note is retired with mark confirmed absent.
